mechanism_narrative: INSR-MET forced proximity via flexible_GS4 linker (~20 Å) enables transphosphorylation where INSR kinase phosphorylates MET juxtamembrane docking sites (Y1003, Y1234/1235) and MET kinase phosphorylates INSR juxtamembrane/IRS-binding sites (Y960, Y1146/1150/1151). This biased co-clustering preferentially recruits GRB2-SHC1-SOS (MAPK), GAB1-PIK3R1 (PI3K/AKT), and IRS1/2 (IRS-PI3K) adaptors while sterically excluding PLCG1/2 (Ca2+ branch) and NCK1/VAV1 (actin remodeling). The resulting biased output shifts aged muscle toward a young transcriptional phenotype: upregulating contractile/structural genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN) and downregulating aged IEGs (EGR1, FOS, JUN) and atrophy markers (MYF5, MYH9, TTN, NEB).
